Reviewing event overlap and impulse recovery

Source: EVENT_ALIGNMENT_OVERLAP_GUIDE.md

This change makes overlapping event windows auditable and preserves missing data. It does not separate neighboring neural responses or introduce a joint event model. For the primary analysis, retain overlapping epochs, inspect their support, and assess the fitted inverse’s temporal spread using a specified generating model.

What changed

  1. Alignment interpolates each unit (usually a voxel) within its valid source segments before computing the requested group’s mean, median, and SD. Adjacent source samples must both be finite and uncensored. An explicit missing row blocks interpolation; deleted acquisitions create a gap when the bracket exceeds max_gap, which defaults to the acquisition TR.
  2. Every output value includes contributor counts, reasons for unavailable contributors, acquisition-time IDs, and the maximum distinct-epoch reuse of those IDs within the returned grouping.
  3. Trial-grouped output includes neighboring event times, simultaneous-event counts, requested-window overlap counts, distances to run edges, and the policy.
  4. deconvolution_impulse_diagnostics() measures recovery and spread into other windows under fixed linear deconvolution settings. It never tunes settings or z-scores each impulse.

Unmissing mean estimates remain equivalent to the previous interpolate-after- aggregation approach on common grids, up to floating-point precision. With missing contributors they can change intentionally: interpolation between two means based on different voxels no longer supplies a nonexistent voxel response. Off-grid median and SD also change intentionally: they now summarize interpolated unit values, rather than interpolating the medians/SDs of source distributions.

Existing output files are not automatically invalidated. Regenerate alignment outputs (overwrite = TRUE for run_decon_alignment) to adopt this behavior.

Run a complete review example

From the repository root:

OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 Rscript --vanilla \
  inst/examples/event_overlap_review.R /tmp/overlap-review

The script loads this checkout when pkgload is available, otherwise the installed package. It writes:

  • alignment_allow.csv, alignment_truncate.csv, and alignment_exclude.csv;
  • source_clock.csv, mapping source IDs to absolute acquisition times;
  • impulse_recovery.csv, with one status and recovery summary per injected event;
  • source_target_windows.csv, with directed source-to-target window metrics;
  • impulse_recovery_uncentered.csv and source_target_windows_uncentered.csv, providing a comparison with measured-run centering disabled;
  • impulse_timeseries.csv, frozen_settings.rds, and overlap_review.png.

Inspect the middle event’s alignment: the deliberately censored interval remains missing even with half-TR output. In the recovery experiment, only the selected source is injected in each simulation. A nonzero estimate in another trial’s window therefore describes spread of that injected event under the specified model, without any actual activity from the neighboring trial.

Alignment policies

Policy Behavior Intended use
allow Retain the full requested window and available interpolation padding. Main analysis with overlap annotations.
truncate Retain source samples strictly after the closest supplied earlier collision and before the closest later collision. Compatibility with previous collision settings; sensitivity analysis.
exclude Return a missing epoch if its closed requested window intersects any other target epoch’s requested window. Conservative whole-epoch sensitivity analysis.

overlap_policy = NULL preserves explicit legacy intent: collision columns select truncate, otherwise the policy is allow. Set allow explicitly to retain windows even when collision columns are supplied. truncate with no collision columns has no truncation bounds.

exclude compares requested target windows, not interpolation padding and not other event types. Touching endpoints count as an intersection; both affected epochs are excluded. Simultaneous target onsets remain distinct trial rows under allow/truncate, and are excluded under exclude. Strict truncation considers only strictly earlier/later collisions, matching the previous implementation.

neighbor_events controls timing annotations independently of censorship. Supply columns such as c("cue", "response", "feedback"). The exact target event record is omitted from its own neighbor search; other event records, including another event type on the same trial, are retained. Simultaneous counts count records. Window-overlap counts always compare target epochs, regardless of this setting.

Neither truncation nor exclusion establishes physiological isolation. Even nonintersecting requested windows can use the same interpolation brackets. Midpoint allocation is not implemented as a presumed decontamination procedure.

Supplying validity and inspecting support

aligned <- get_medusa_interpolated_ts(
  object, event = "feedback", time_before = -3, time_after = 5,
  group_by = c("trial", "region"), output_resolution = 0.5,
  overlap_policy = "allow", neighbor_events = c("cue", "response", "feedback"),
  valid_col = "usable", max_gap = object$tr, time_audit = TRUE
)

The optional usable column must be logical in the source time-series table. FALSE and NA make that row unavailable for all value columns while retaining its time. Without a mask, nonfinite values remain unavailable independently for each value column. Retain acquisition rows and mark them invalid whenever possible. For deleted rows, max_gap is the longest allowed source bracket in seconds; it is independent of the requested output resolution. Increasing it can bridge deleted rows, but cannot bridge explicitly invalid rows. There is no extrapolation.

For a value named decon, these columns describe each output lag:

Field Meaning
decon_mean, decon_median, decon_sd Statistics of finite interpolated unit estimates; SD requires two units.
decon_n, decon_n_total Available and represented contributors. With trial grouping, contributors are units; when pooling trials, they are unit/epoch combinations.
decon_n_censored Contributors blocked by an explicit validity mask at the requested sample or bracket.
decon_n_missing Contributors blocked by nonfinite values, including placeholder units in missing/excluded epochs. Check epoch_status to distinguish the latter.
decon_n_gap Contributors blocked by a deleted-row bracket wider than max_gap.
decon_n_outside Contributors lacking a source sample or bracketing support, including run/collision boundaries.
decon_source_ids Semicolon-separated sorted acquisition-time IDs used by finite contributors; empty when none contribute.
decon_source_max_epochs Largest number of distinct epochs using any of those acquisition-time IDs within the same value/output group; zero with no contributors. Repeated lags within one epoch do not inflate it.

The available count plus the four unavailable-reason counts equals the total. epoch_status summarizes lag availability of any value’s finite mean, not a complete contributor cohort; inspect per-value counts for changing support. When several reasons could apply to a bracket, explicit censoring takes precedence, then nonfinite values, then excessive bracket duration. Exact valid samples remain available even next to a gap. Duplicate times within a unit/epoch are errors.

IDs index sorted observed acquisition times within the input run, not voxels. Reuse indicates a shared acquisition time, and does not assert identical voxel subsets contributed to each epoch. The source_clock attribute maps IDs to times. It is present on raw event_lock_ts() results and interpolated data. For batch alignment, alignment_file disambiguates source files; the combined clock includes file/identity columns and is written to <out_file>.sources.csv. The existing file_status attribute and <out_file>.files.csv continue to record file failures. IDs are not globally unique across files. No neural independence is implied by a reuse count of one.

Per-trial fields are align_onset, align_previous_event, align_next_event, align_simultaneous_n, align_window_overlap_n, align_run_start_distance, align_run_end_distance, and align_overlap_policy. Run distances are signed; an onset outside the run has a negative distance to one edge. Missing onsets have missing timing annotations. overlap_excluded is the new epoch status; other status meanings are retained. If trial is omitted from group_by, statistics can pool epochs, but trial-level annotations and epoch statuses are not attached. The align_* names and internal .align_* fields are reserved in source data.

The same four settings (overlap_policy, valid_col, neighbor_events, max_gap) can be included in an alignment list passed to evt_align_decon_files() or run_decon_alignment(). Validity masks apply to post-deconvolution alignment. They do not refit deconvolution with masked BOLD observations, nor repair effects of invalid BOLD samples that already entered an inverse fit. Observation-weighted forward modeling remains separate work.

Measuring temporal spread with frozen settings

recovery <- deconvolution_impulse_diagnostics(
  event_data = trials, onset = "feedback", trial = "trial",
  n_time = n_volumes, tr = TR, time_offset = acquisition_offset,
  kernel = selected_hrf, lambda = selected_lambda,
  backend = "cpp", penalty = "diff2", prewhiten_rho = selected_rho,
  input_scale = fitted_bold_sd, input_demean = TRUE,
  tail_padding = length(selected_hrf),
  time_before = -3, time_after = 5,
  source_trials = trials$trial[unique(c(1, ceiling(nrow(trials) / 2), nrow(trials)))],
  return_timeseries = TRUE
)

Use the actual fitted settings from the run/voxel or a documented representative operator. lambda is required. kernel is the selected HRF, not a candidate grid; prewhiten_rho is fixed rather than re-estimated. The supported backends are cpp, r, and scalar wiener. Adaptive PSD and Bush estimates are not fixed linear operators and are not supported by this diagnostic.

For a fixed operator, the relevant response is D H x, including the specified centering and boundary treatment. input_scale uses a frozen positive divisor; outputs are multiplied back into injected-impulse units, so changing this divisor alone does not manufacture a different recovery gain. input_demean = TRUE applies the same linear measured-run mean-removal operation to each generated column before padding. It does not divide each impulse by its own SD.

tail_padding = 0 is the standalone finite-run case. Use the original kernel length to reproduce the wrapper’s appended zero BOLD observations. The diagnostic retains that boundary assumption so its effects can be assessed; it does not fix it. A different forward_kernel tests a specified HRF mismatch; both generating and inverse HRFs are normalized to unit sum, consistent with the linear API.

Each selected source event is injected separately with zero pre-run history. Off-grid onsets distribute unit mass between their two surrounding acquisition bins. Thus the injected samples sum to one, and area is tr; this approximation does not claim sub-TR neural resolution. truth_at_onset records the interpolated grid truth, which can be less than one off-grid. onset_gain divides recovery by that grid truth, while mass_gain compares summed recovered samples with unit injected mass. Peak timing is reported relative to the specified onset and is limited by the acquisition grid. With input_demean = TRUE, mean removal adds a run-wide baseline component to the impulse response. Signed recovered mass is no longer expected to equal one; pre-onset and distant-window activity can include this centering effect as well as inverse-filter spreading. The example compares centered and uncentered inputs so these effects can be inspected separately. Missing/outside onsets and impulses producing zero or constant observed BOLD retain statuses and missing recovery metrics. Events outside the measured acquisition span are not injected, even though a pre-run event can physiologically affect BOLD acquired later.

The directed windows table compares each selected source with every target window. It reports finite lag counts, absolute-area and signed-area sums, maximum absolute response, and window_l1_ratio relative to that source’s own window. Area summaries are rectangular grid sums times output_resolution over available lags. Compare coverage before comparing areas near run edges. Ratios can exceed one, and overlapping windows count some response repeatedly: they are not fractions of measured neural attribution and need not sum to one.

No noise, RPE values, automatic tuning, observation-mask refitting, or uncertainty intervals are included. These are conditional operator diagnostics. Validating scientific recovery still requires realistic HRFs, noise, actual schedules and RPE sequences, and a separate evaluation of the full parameter-selection process. For large schedules, begin with selected early/middle/late source events: window output grows as selected sources times all target events. Full time series are optional and scale as selected sources times measured volumes. Impulse fits are batched; alignment processes one output group at a time and uses shared matrix brackets for common rectangular grids, with a per-unit fallback for ragged grids.

Review checklist

  • Verify behavioral onsets, time_offset, discarded volumes, and acquisition timing use the same clock.
  • Inspect the example’s missing interval and compare counts with the original mask.
  • Confirm source IDs resolve through source_clock and repeated lags do not increase distinct-epoch reuse counts.
  • Compare policies and report changes in included trials and contributors by lag.
  • Inspect whether exclusions/support relate to RPE, reaction time, or condition.
  • Compare impulse recovery across run positions, lambda/HRF choices, and padding assumptions. Do not select a pipeline by maximizing its observed RPE association.
  • Account for repeated acquisitions and temporal dependence in downstream inference; avoid treating overlapping epoch rows as independent observations.

Validation performed

The package installed successfully in an isolated library. Focused installed- package checks passed 74 test cases and 708 assertions, with no failures, errors, or warnings. They cover explicit/deleted gaps, masks, contributor changes, simultaneous events, policy boundaries, source clocks, empty clocks, legacy/custom identity mappings, multivariate output, native extraction/geometry, and the existing linear/voxelwise regressions. Matrix interpolation agrees with the per-unit oracle on masked grids. Impulse recovery agrees with a dense finite inverse, and directed window metrics agree with independently sampled responses. Tests also cover fixed centering/scaling/whitening/padding, batches, off-grid onsets, missing/outside/unobserved impulses, and specified HRF mismatch.

A two-worker installed-package check matched serial estimates, contributor counts, overlap annotations, and source clocks for both allow and truncate policies. R/Rd parsing, Rd checks, and whitespace checks passed. The review script ran and generated the documented tables and plot. The full unrelated package suite and participant-data scientific validation were not run.
